title: A persuasive recommendation
prompt: Recommend an imagined farm or nature visit for a local group. Explain the experiences visitors could enjoy and how the visit could benefit the host community. Support your recommendation with clear reasons.
checks: I used persuasive but accurate language.
I checked present and past habit forms.

title: An opinion about adventure programmes
prompt: Give your opinion of survival or adventure programmes. Discuss one possible benefit and one concern, then explain whether you would watch or take part. Use comparisons and examples.

title: A balanced personal description
prompt: Describe an imagined person and the kind of work that might suit them. Give reasons based on preferences and skills, avoiding the assumption that all introverts or extroverts behave alike. Use relative clauses.
checks: I gave specific preferences and skills.

title: An argument about teamwork
prompt: Argue for either team activities or individual activities in an imagined class or workplace. Explain two benefits and acknowledge one possible concern. Support your position with examples.
checks: I used emphasis and pronouns accurately.

title: A supported opinion
prompt: Give your opinion about phone use in an imagined public setting. Describe a problem and a possible solution. Use a conditional and connecting expressions to distinguish your view from other views.
checks: I described a problem and solution.

title: A story with an unexpected ending
prompt: Write an imagined story in which an assumption turns out to be wrong. Use a variety of past tenses, linking expressions and reporting verbs. Make the ending follow clearly from the events.
checks: I connected the unexpected ending to the story.

title: A for-and-against essay
prompt: Discuss whether spending money on experiences is better than spending it on possessions. Give arguments on both sides, then state your view. Use imagined examples rather than unsupported statistics.

title: A polite complaint
prompt: Write a polite complaint about an imagined product or service that did not meet expectations. Give the relevant details, explain the problem and ask for a reasonable solution.
checks: I checked tone and future forms.

title: A practical tips article
prompt: Write an article giving three tips for starting or ending a conversation politely. Give each tip a short heading and explain how to use it. Keep parallel wording in lists.
checks: I used a useful title and headings.

title: A professional profile
prompt: Write a short professional profile for an imagined person or small organization. Explain its work, strengths and experience using a clear professional tone. Avoid vague exaggerated claims.
checks: I included relevant strengths and experience.
I checked gerunds and verb complements.

title: A persuasive argument with evidence
prompt: Write a persuasive argument about an imagined product or service. Acknowledge an opposing opinion, then support your position with concrete features and examples. Avoid unverified health or safety promises.

title: A performance review
prompt: Review an imagined film, play, concert or other performance. Describe what worked and what did not, explaining reasons and results with words such as therefore, so and as a result.
checks: I described specific aspects of the performance.
I used adjectives and adverbs accurately.
